newsitem.title: USA: Clinton orders $112 million for drug war.
newsitem.headline: Clinton orders $112 million for drug war.

text.p: President Bill Clinton announced on Tuesday his intention to give $112 million worth of military equipment and training to Colombia, Venezuela, Peru, Mexico and Caribbean countries to fight the drug war.
In a statement, the White House said the aid "will assist our allies in stopping the flow of drugs at the source, before they reach our shores."

The White House made the announcement in New York, where Clinton was attending the U.N. General Assembly. Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole has accused Clinton of taking a lax attitude toward controlling drug abuse in America.

Clinton said he intended to send $112 million in helicopters, surveillance aircraft, boats, vehicles, communications gear and field equipment for Mexico, Colombia, Venezuela, Peru and nations in the eastern Caribbean.

The equipment is to be taken out of Defence Department stocks. For budget purposes, the White House said $75 million would be taken out of spending for the current fiscal year and the rest out of the budget for fiscal 1997, which starts Oct. 1.

The White House said Clinton had notified Congress on Sept. 14 of his intent to direct the money to the drug war. Congressional approval is not needed, although members could conceivably act against the 1997 spending, since the budget for that fiscal year is not yet completed.
The 1997 portion of Clinton's drug plan includes sending Mexico's military 53 UH-1H helicopters, spare parts and training and four C-26 observation aircraft.
Clinton also asked other nations that produce chemicals used to make illegal drugs to join in creating an informal arrangement to control drug exports.
"Through cooperative and complementary approaches with other nations, we will limit and deny access to these chemicals to those who would use them to produce illegal drugs," the White House said.
